references.text: Aaron asked the people to take off their gold jewelry, which they then gave him. This is the background for Aaron's excuse in verse 24.
Aaron shaped the gold with a graving tool and made a cast calf. His explanation in verse 24 that the calf 'came out' of the fire is a distortion of the truth.
Moses asks Aaron what the people did to him that led them into such great sin. Verse 24 is Aaron's answer to this question.
Adam blamed Eve when he was confronted with his sin, just as Aaron blames the people and downplays his own role.
Proverbs teaches that the one who hides their sins will not prosper. Aaron's attempt to hide his role in making the golden calf is an example of this.
Complementary account of the same event showing the complete destruction of the idol.
Theological contrast between consecrating gold for the Lord's house and misusing gold for idolatry.
